stem: A client has continuous generalized convulsive seizure activity lasting 6 minutes. Which action is most consistent with current treatment guidance?

options.A: Continue observation until seizure activity reaches 30 minutes because treatment before that point can interfere with spontaneous seizure termination.
options.B: Begin first-line benzodiazepine therapy promptly because the AES initial-treatment phase for ongoing convulsive seizure activity begins at 5 minutes.
options.C: Delay antiseizure treatment until the client returns to baseline because medication is indicated only when repeated seizures occur after consciousness returns.
options.D: Treat the event as a simple self-limited seizure and provide supportive care only because continuous convulsions do not meet treatment criteria before 10 minutes.

rationale: The American Epilepsy Society convulsive status epilepticus algorithm places 0–5 minutes in the stabilization phase and 5–20 minutes in the initial-therapy phase, when a benzodiazepine is recommended as initial therapy. At 6 minutes of continuous generalized convulsions, prompt benzodiazepine treatment is therefore appropriate. A delays treatment until an obsolete 30-minute threshold, while C and D delay treatment despite ongoing convulsive activity.
educational_objective: Treat continuous generalized convulsive seizure activity that persists to 5 minutes as requiring prompt initial benzodiazepine therapy rather than waiting for prolonged seizure duration.
source_document_title: Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults
source_version_date: January 2016 guideline remains AES-listed current foundational guidance while an updated Status Epilepticus guideline is in development in 2026

source_claim_supported: For ongoing convulsive seizure activity, AES starts the initial-treatment phase at 5 minutes and recommends benzodiazepine therapy as the initial treatment of choice.

source_original.stem: A client has continuous generalized convulsive seizure activity lasting 6 minutes. Which action is most consistent with current treatment guidance?

options.A: Continue observation until seizure activity reaches 30 minutes, because treatment before that point can interfere with spontaneous seizure termination.
options.B: Begin first-line benzodiazepine therapy promptly, because the AES initial-treatment phase for ongoing convulsive seizure activity starts at about 5 minutes.
options.C: Delay antiseizure treatment until the client returns to baseline, because medication is indicated only when repeated seizures occur after consciousness returns.
options.D: Treat the event as a simple self-limited seizure and provide supportive care only, because continuous convulsions do not meet emergency criteria before 10 minutes.

source_original.rationale: At 6 minutes of continuous generalized convulsive activity, the seizure has entered the AES initial-treatment phase, when a benzodiazepine is recommended promptly. Option B follows that treatment algorithm. Option A waits until 30 minutes and delays effective treatment. Option C delays medication until recovery despite ongoing convulsions. Option D incorrectly treats persistent 6-minute convulsive activity as an event needing supportive care alone.
source_original.source_detail: American Epilepsy Society evidence-based convulsive status epilepticus treatment algorithm — stabilization phase 0–5 minutes; initial therapy phase 5–20 minutes; benzodiazepines are recommended initial therapy for ongoing generalized convulsive seizure activity. AES evidence-based convulsive-status guideline remains the listed foundational treatment guidance in 2026 while an updated status-epilepticus guideline is in development; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. correction_summary: Retained key and exact 5-minute treatment threshold. Removed the hedge 'about' because the AES algorithm explicitly labels the initial-therapy phase as 5–20 minutes; currentness was verified against AES's 2026 guideline catalog showing this guideline remains listed while an update is in development.

audit_findings.source_authority: AES evidence-based guideline and official 2026 clinical-guidance catalog.
audit_findings.currentness: 2016 guideline remains AES-listed while replacement systematic review/guideline is still in development.
audit_findings.exact_locator: AES treatment algorithm phases 0–5 and 5–20 minutes.
audit_findings.claim_audit: 5-minute threshold and benzodiazepine initial therapy are direct guideline statements; no drug dose or route was added.

distractor_audit.C: Ongoing convulsions require treatment before recovery.
distractor_audit.D: 10-minute delay is unsupported for generalized convulsive status in this algorithm.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B matches the AES phase-based algorithm.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address timing/initial response with no second defensible answer.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Verified that an updated AES guideline has not yet replaced the cited algorithm and retained only current supported precision.
